phase: PHASE 19 — MACRO DATA ACQUISITION & INTEGRITY AUDIT
verdict_rationale:
All three mandatory macroeconomic series (DFII10, DTWEXBGS, T10YIE) were successfully acquired from official Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED endpoints spanning 2003/2006 to 2026. Gold data integrity confirms 984 institutional daily sessions (276 M5 bars standard) with 0 duplicate timestamps and 0 invalid OHLC relationships. Under a conservative 1-business-day publication lag with holiday forward-fill (limit=3 days), exactly 984 of 984 gold sessions (100.0%) possess complete macro data, providing a statistically viable N/D ratio of 196.8:1 for D <= 5 features.

HOWEVER, point-in-time limitations remain: (1) FRED daily CSVs record observation dates rather than exact intraday release timestamps; (2) Historical vintages (from ALFRED) were not captured, meaning DTWEXBGS broad dollar trade-weight revisions reflect retrospective current-vintage adjustments; and (3) DTWEXBGS is a broad trade-weighted index, not the traded ICE DXY index. While applying a 1-business-day lag eliminates same-day execution look-ahead risk, historical revision limitations cannot be erased without vintage reconstruction. Therefore, the data cannot be declared fully point-in-time safe.

macro_acquisition_audit.critical_distinction_dtwexbgs_vs_dxy: DTWEXBGS is the Federal Reserve Board's Nominal Broad Trade-Weighted U.S. Dollar Index, calculated against 26 trading partner currencies with annually reweighted trade weights. It is NOT the ICE U.S. Dollar Index (DXY), which is a 6-currency fixed-weight tradable index. DTWEXBGS is labeled correctly across all artifacts.

gold_data_integrity_audit.price_convention: HistData Bid Quotes Only (Synthetic Ask modeled via ExecutionCostModel)

institutional_daily_sessions.session_definition: 18:00 NY to 17:00 NY next day (23 trading hours + 1h rollover pause)
institutional_daily_sessions.h288_calendar_day_refutation: H=288 M5 bars represents 24.0 hours of continuous trading without closure. Because gold markets close 1 hour daily at 17:00 NY and over weekends, rolling 288 bars induces a 12-bar (1-hour) phase shift relative to NY daily settlement every day. An institutional gold trading day contains 276 M5 bars.

conservative_lag_policy.description: Macro observation date <= entry date - 1 calendar day. Guarantees publication >= 24h prior to trade entry.
conservative_lag_policy.holiday_justification: Carrying the last known closing yield/index across weekend/holiday market closures (up to 3 calendar days) reflects authentic institutional practice where non-traded assets retain their last settlement price until trading resumes.

same_day_release_policy.description: Macro observation date <= entry date. Assumes daily release by 17:00 NY is available for 18:00 NY entry.
same_day_release_policy.point_in_time_risk: Same-day evening entry assumes publication by 17:00 NY. If FRED or Treasury servers experience release delays, trades placed at 18:00 NY incur look-ahead bias.

sample_size_evaluation_for_phase20.sample_sufficiency_justification: With N = 984 daily sessions and D <= 5 explanatory features, the observation-to-feature ratio is 196.8:1 (> 150:1 requirement). This sample is statistically viable for evaluating parsimonious linear macro models across chronological walk-forward folds.
